outcome: weaning readiness off nasal continuous positive airway pressure (nCPAP)
cohort: The study included 39 premature infants with a gestational age of less than 33 weeks.
finding: Point-of-care lung ultrasound (POC-LUS) was found to predict weaning readiness off nCPAP in premature infants, with expLUSsc achieving 88% sensitivity and 90% specificity, which improved to 95% sensitivity and 90% specificity when lung tidal recruitment (LTR) was added.
